voiceover:
[conversational] Your AI-built landing page screams "AI made this", and visitors notice.

And fixing it takes one extra file most people skip.

Sparkle logos, "Revolutionize Your Workflow", a fake "10,000% ROI".

[confident] It's called Anti Slop. Free, open source, MIT licensed. On their GitHub page you'll see almost 40 rules, and a pass or fail report before anything ships.

Step 1, open a terminal in your project folder. Step 2, run npx skills add miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop and pick Claude Code. Step 3, start a session and choose "During" to build, or "After" to audit an existing page.

[serious] It's a filter, not a designer. It stops fake stats and words like "Seamless", but it won't give you a look.

[whispers] The extra file is DESIGN.md. Describe your look there, and that's what makes it yours.

Worth it if you ship AI-built pages.

What's the cringiest line AI ever wrote on your site? Send this to the friend who builds every page with AI. Hack saved?

pick.tool: Anti Slop skill for Claude Code (free, open-source)
pick.angle: Your AI-built landing page screams 'AI made this', and visitors notice. Here's the free rule set that fixes it before you publish.
pick.why: 102k views and 5,361 likes (about 5% like rate) on a 42s reel shows strong resonance. It's on-mix for landing pages and conversion, and the 'AI slop' negative hook is true and checkable. We can show real before/after pages and the skill's rules on screen.

research.tool: Anti Slop ("antislop"): Rules for AI Coding Agents, by miqdadbadjuber. It is an open-source skill pack with a core skill plus UI, copywriting, human/accessibility, mobile-layout and code-comment skills.
research.availability: Free, MIT-licensed, open source. It is a text rulebook that runs inside a coding agent: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Cline, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot and others. It is not region-limited. A single antislop.md file can also be pasted into any chat window.
steps: Open a terminal in your project folder.
Run: npx skills add miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop (the skills CLI then asks which agent and scope to install for; pick Claude Code).
Alternative inside Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add https://github.com/miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop, then /plugin install antislop@anti-slop.
Alternative single file: curl -o antislop.md https://raw.githubusercontent.com/miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop/main/antislop.md. This works in any chat, but the gate is not enforced there.
Optional but recommended for UI you plan to ship: add a DESIGN.md to the project describing the look you want. The README says it is mandatory for UI you intend to ship.

Start a session. By default the agent asks which mode to use. 'During' follows the rules while building and ends with the Delivery Gate report. 'After' audits an existing page: it writes a numbered findings list, you approve which to fix, then it gives a follow-up report.
If Claude Code was already running, you may need to run /reload-skills (per the qai.io listing).
facts: The GitHub README currently says: "40 mandatory rules (R-01 to R-40) in three tiers: Hard Gate, Purpose-Gate, and Quality Locks." Older README versions, antislop.ai.id and most articles still say 38 rules (R-01 to R-38).
The Delivery Gate is a mandatory PASS/FAIL report in four blocks, run before anything ships. Each PASS must be backed by concrete evidence, and delivery without a clean gate counts as a failure.

There are six skills: antislop (core, always loaded), antislop-ui, antislop-copywriting (headlines, CTAs, tone, fake stats), antislop-human (contrast, keyboard, focus, states), antislop-layoutmobile, and antislop-code (which AI comments to remove and which to keep).
The repo is MIT-licensed and written in JavaScript. At the time of the search it showed about 8.6k stars and 580 forks. The reel's "7.6k" is outdated.
The README says it is "a filter, not a style guide": no prescribed colors, fonts or layouts. Direction comes from your DESIGN.md.
The README's before/after example describes a generic landing page with a sparkle logo, a "NEXT-GEN AI 2.0 beta" pill, and a fake terminal reporting 0.0001ms latency.

The Hard Gate tier includes honesty, function and accessibility rules such as fake stats and dead links (from the v2.0.0 release notes). The Delivery Gate also checks for AI buzzwords such as AI Powered, Seamless, Revolutionary and Cutting Edge.
Supported agents per the README FAQ: Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, OpenCode, Cursor, Cline, Amp, Gemini CLI, Hermes, GitHub Copilot, Kimi Code, Pi and Oh My Pi.
Other install routes: npx antislop-ai (an interactive installer) and the site antislop.ai.id.
The latest release at the time of the search was v3.2.21, dated 16 Oct. The qai.io listing shows the skill last changed 1 Nov 2026.
do_not_claim: Do not say "7.6k stars". It is now about 8.5–8.6k and rising. Say "8k+ stars", or leave the number out.
Do not say "40 rules" without checking: the repo README and GUIDE say 40, but antislop.ai.id and several articles still say 38. Use "almost 40 rules" or "dozens of rules".

Do not say it makes your design original or beautiful by itself. The README says it removes slop and stops there, and that a DESIGN.md supplies the direction. Without DESIGN.md the agent labels UI work a "draft without direction".
Do not say "the agent is forced to produce a pass/fail report" as a guarantee. The gate is an instruction the agent follows, and the guide admits nothing enforces it in plain chat apps.
Do not say it is a single "rules file". The main install is a set of six skills. The single antislop.md is a fallback.

Do not claim it works by running plain "npx antislop". The README says that npm name belongs to a different package. The correct commands are npx skills add miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop or npx antislop-ai.
Do not claim the 'zero comments in code' angle. The code skill removes generic AI comments but keeps valuable ones.

Do not say the tool is endorsed by Anthropic. It is a third-party community skill. There are also several similarly named but unrelated 'anti-slop' skills (hardikpandya/stop-slop, Nutlope/hallmark, rand/cc-polymath) that should not be confused with this one.
criticism: It is a filter, not a designer. The README's own 'before/after' notes the plain filter result is 'the slop is gone, but so is the direction', and you must write a DESIGN.md yourself for a finished look.
Compliance relies on the AI following instructions. The guide says that in a chat paste, the rules are context and nothing enforces them or runs the gate.
Extra reading load: the UI skill alone is 344 lines (28.4 KB), and the core plus five skills add context tokens. The skill loads on demand, per the TypingMind listing.
The rules reflect one author's taste, for example banning em dashes and certain gradients. That is not a universal standard.
The project is young. GitGem tracks it from 12 Aug 2026, and the release history shows rapid change, with multiple releases per week in Sept and Oct. Rule counts and install paths are still changing.
Third-party advice (TypingMind) says to read the skill source before installing any skill. That is sensible, since skills are instructions your agent executes.

ui.platforms: Terminal / CLI (macOS, Windows, Linux) plus GitHub web pages. The skill runs in coding-agent CLIs and IDE agents, not in a phone app.

The skills CLI then shows an interactive prompt for choosing the agent (e.g. Claude Code) and the install scope. I could not verify the exact wording or layout of the prompt. Show it only as a real recording, or keep the mock minimal.

Claude Code session: a terminal chat interface. After installation the agent asks, at the start of a session, whether to use 'During' or 'After' mode (per the GUIDE). Skills are stored under .claude/skills/antislop (per qai.io). The final output ends with a PASS/FAIL list with one line per rule and evidence (e.g. 'R-26 PASS: all buttons have real href/onClick; no dead controls').

Result view: a landing page that has no sparkle logo, no 'Revolutionize Your Workflow'-style buzzword copy, and no invented ROI numbers, shown beside the slop version. The README's before/after images show this contrast.

research.visuals: Best shown as a split screen of a slop landing page (sparkle logo, buzzword headline, '10,000% ROI') against the cleaned-up version, using the repo's own before/after images. Add the install command in a terminal and the PASS/FAIL gate report at the end of a Claude Code session. The real agent output can only be shown with a real screen recording. The terminal install prompt and the gate report are not visible on any public page.
research.notes: The skill exists and the reel's install command is correct. The reel's numbers are stale: stars are now about 8.6k, not 7.6k, and the rule count is 40 on GitHub but 38 on antislop.ai.id and in articles. I rated this 'adjust' because the angle 'fixes it before you publish' overpromises. It removes slop (fake stats, buzzwords, generic UI patterns) and runs a PASS/FAIL gate, but originality needs your own DESIGN.md. Suggested framing: 'it stops your AI from inventing fake stats and buzzword copy, and makes it prove it with a checklist. Add your own DESIGN.md for a look that is yours.' The page text 'Revolutionize Your Workflow' and '10,000% ROI' is the reel's own example and not a quote from the repo. The repo's own example is 'NEXT-GEN AI 2.0 beta' and '0.0001ms latency'. Do not confuse it with other 'anti-slop' skills: Nutlope/hallmark, hardikpandya/stop-slop (text only), rand/cc-polymath. The creator's handle is miqdadbadjuber (Indonesia), and the repo exists in an Indonesian version too (ANTISLOP-ID.md), which suits the Indonesian audience.
